program.intent: Convert date, time, and timezone into epoch-microseconds and store as one numeric value.
program.code:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

def forward(groups):
    day, month, year, time, sp1, tz_offset = groups
    text = f"{day} {month} {year} {time}"
    dt = datetime.strptime(text, '%d %b %Y %H:%M:%S')
    tz_hours = int(tz_offset[:3])
    tz_minutes = int(tz_offset[0] + tz_offset[3:])
    offset = timedelta(hours=tz_hours, minutes=tz_minutes)
    dt_utc = dt - offset
    return {'stored': [int(dt_utc.timestamp() * 1000000)], 'layout': [len(sp1)]}

def inverse(record):
    micros = int(record['stored'][0])
    layout = record.get('layout', [])
    sp1_len = layout[0]
    dt_utc = datetime.fromtimestamp(micros / 1000000)
    tz_offset = timedelta(seconds=dt_utc.utcoffset().total_seconds())
    offset_hours, remainder = divmod(tz_offset.total_seconds(), 3600)
    offset_minutes = abs(remainder // 60)
    tz_str = f"{int(offset_hours):+03}{int(offset_minutes):02}"
    dt = dt_utc + tz_offset
    return f"{dt.strftime('%d/%b/%Y:%H:%M:%S')}" + (' ' * sp1_len) + tz_str
